newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issuance activity to remain thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issuance activity to remain thin.

text.p: Corporate bond issuance has tapered off and dealers said activity is expected to remain at these levels well into the new year as market players begin to head out for the holidays, dealers said.
"The (new issue) market's very quiet," said one syndicate source. "Looking ahead there's no real calendar but I'm sure we'll see a lot of business in the new year."
Dealers said with two holidays falling in the middle of the week, activity should remain thin as well as issuance.
Next Wednesday, the U.S. credit market will close in observance of the Christmas Day holiday.
Dealers said the issue was very well received by the market and was quoted tighter at spread of 133 basis points shortly after pricing.
Meanwhile, First Tennessee National is expected to issue $100 million in 30-year debt with a call feature in the tenth year via Goldman Sachs & Co, dealers said.
Also, BTC Capital Securities is expected to set a $250 million issue due 2006 via Bear Stearns.
Meanwhile, among deals expected in the new calendar year are Italy's $1.0 billion 10-year global issue, and State Development Bank of China's $300 million 10-year yankee debt offering, dealers said.
Also, Disney & Co is rumored to come to market in the new year with a $500 million 10-year debt offering of its own, syndicate sources said.
Currently, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond is off 2/32 at 98-26/32 to yield 6.65 percent off from Wednesday's 6.70 percent yield at the close.
Also, players will begin their holiday festivities a little earlier as the Public Securities Association (PSA) has recommended an early close on Tuesday.
Dealers said amid the quiet activity a sprinkling of preferred issues may still come to market.

So far on Friday, Mellon Capital II, a unit of Mellon Bank Corp issued $500 million in 7.995 percent capital securities due 2027 to yield 7.995 or 137.5 basis points over Treasuries via lead manager, Merrill Lynch & Co.
